title: How the Miami Heat saved the season after a terrible start
summary: The Miami Heat ended last season in an awkward spot. For the fourth straight year, they found themselves in the NBA Play-In Tournament. Unfortunately, this was the first time they couldn’t make it out. They have a S-Tier leading man calling the shots, a battle-tested defensive anchor, and a culture of winning in the ugliest […]
content: (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Heat ended last season in an awkward spot. For the fourth straight year, they found themselves in the NBA Play-In Tournament. Unfortunately, this was the first time they couldn’t make it out. They have a S-Tier leading man calling the shots, a battle-tested defensive anchor , and a culture of winning in the ugliest ways possible. Their roster, while nothing special, was far from the dregs of the association. It contained a good blend of young bucks and proven veterans. If the injury gods smiled in their favor and a couple of prospects took meaningful steps forward, the Heat could have run it back and flirted with 50 wins. And with their knack for upsets, maybe a postseason series victory would have followed. However, the Heat, like the Minnesota Timberwolves , remembered that they didn’t come to the table to nickel and dime their way through the nights. In Miami, they play for keeps. Win big, or go bankrupt trying. So, when Giannis Antetokounmpo finally became available, the Heat swung for the fences – trading the farm in the hopes that the singular excellence of the former two-time MVP , coupled with Bam Adebayo and the scrapes that remained would be enough to vault the team into true contention. Through nine games, it looked like they would be filing for Chapter 7. The Heat were 3-6 and floundering, while their contemporaries (the Detroit Pistons, Boston Celtics, and Philadelphia 76ers) were thriving out the gate. But fast forward to today, and it looks like the big bet they placed may have been the right call. What Changed For The Miami Heat? After their 10-point win over the depleted Oklahoma City Thunder, the Heat are winners of their last seven games and now sit at No. 6 in the Eastern Conference – fully within striking distance of the conference’s upper echelon. In a team sport like basketball, it’s foolish to point to one variable as the reason for positive change, as so many factors contribute to success, but it is hard not to watch this team and look at the ring leader as the catalyst: Erik Spoelstra. Spoelstra may be the best coach in basketball. Heck, he may be one of the five best coaches that ever lived (we know he’s at least one of the top 15 ). Spoelstra is innovative enough to turn oranges into lemonade. No, that’s not a typo that was missed by my editor. The creative lens Spoelstra is able to analyze the game through literally defies everything we know about the human experience. With an average age of 28.8 years old , the Heat have the second-oldest team in the NBA (behind only the Golden State Warriors). That is bad news bears in today’s game – one that rewards athleticism, pace, and physicality. Spoelstra realized it was time to demote the veterans that most coaches would remain beholden too. His biggest change was taking Andrew Wiggins (31 years old), and putting Pelle Larsson in his place (25). And when he’s been hurt, instead of reverting back to Wiggins, Spoelstra simply plugs in Myron Gardner (25) in his place. A former second rounder and undrafted player in the place of a former first overall pick, NBA champion, and the third-highest paid player on the team’s payroll. Wiggins wasn’t the only casualty. Bobby Portis’ minutes are down, and Tim Hardaway Jr. is basically out of the rotation entirely. Along with Larsson and Gardner, those minutes are being eaten up by the youthful vigor of second round rookie Ryan Conwell (22). Despite hearing 36 names called before his on draft night, Conwell is seventh among rookies in minutes per game (26.2) in their last seven games. Delegating hustle duties to fresher legs lessens the burdens on Antetokounmpo, Adebayo, Klay Thompson, and Davion Mitchell’s shoulders, and enables them to focus more energy on scoring the ball. The Heat’s effective field goal percentage is up 4.8% over the last seven games. Spoelstra has also made a key strategic shift. To start the season, the Heat were doing a lot of hard hedging with ball screens involving their bigs. The idea is that since they start two center-sized players, they could afford for one of them to play these actions more aggressively, since the other one would be there to clean it up. The idea wasn’t a bad one, in theory, but playing this way asks the three guys not involved in the action to do a lot of flying around to cover up the gaps. Antetokounmpo, now in Year 14, has a lot of tread on his tires, and scrambling around possession after possession isn’t necessarily high on his list of priorities. So, instead of trying to fit a square peg into a round hole, Spoelstra scrapped the idea and started switching everything (except actions involving Portis, which the Heat continue to hedge). This asks Antetokounmpo and company to do a lot less rotating around, and it still lets the Heat benefit from their twin tower configuration (when one of them is switched onto the perimeter, the other can still lurk around the painted area). As a result, the Heat are forcing fewer turnovers (the tradeoff of playing a less aggressive style). However, by switching everything, it is easier for them to keep the ball in front of them, and so the Heat’s opponents are shooting far worse from the floor than they were before. And again, it conserves more energy, so the Heat have their legs under them on their own shots. Due to the constraints of the written medium, we can’t dissect ALL of Spoelstra’s game-changing tweaks, but here are a couple of other developments you can see his fingerprint on: convincing Antetokounmpo into operating more off-the-ball, squeezing the last ounce of magic out of Thompson, and gradually helping mold Mitchell from bust to baller. How Good Are The Heat Actually? The good news for the Heat is that there are some aspects that will improve with time. Despite rostering Antetokounmpo and Adebayo – who have 11 All-Defensive Teams between the two of them – Miami is currently 24th in defensive rating. The adjustments the Heat have made with minute allocation and scheme have helped bump them from 26th in this category in their first nine games to 17th in the last seven, but they are still being hurt by some bad luck. This season, the Heat are surrendering a whopping 45.6% on wide open threes (per NBA.com). That is 2.7% than the next highest team, and 6.1% higher than the league average. The Heat under Spoelstra tend to give up more threes in order to prioritize protecting the rim, but defense has nothing to do with how well opponents shoot on open looks. That’s just luck. If/when that number regresses to the mean (no team has allowed higher than 43% on these shots for an entire season), Miami’s defensive rating will automatically improve. Unfortunately, the Heat have also been the beneficiary of some good luck. According to Estimated Plus-Minus, they have had the third-easiest strength of schedule. They have also lost the fourth-fewest dollars to player injuries (per Spotrac). Antetokounmpo and Thompson have only missed one game each. Mitchell and Adebayo have been available for every game. What happens if one or two of those guys is out for an extended stretch? This isn’t a super deep team. More than likely, the conflicting noise between their negative shooting luck and positive schedule/injury history thus far is a wash. To me, the pace this Heat are currently on (51 wins) seems about right. They are a good team that, even with Spoelstra’s magic touch, still has some glaring flaws (on-ball creation, offensive variety, depth) in a conference filled with them. If they draw the first round opponent or injuries cause them to fall into the play-in tournament for the fifth straight year, another early exit could be in their future. But if Spoelstra keeps putting on a coaching clinic in the best league on the planet and Antetokounmpo can stay healthy enough to match him for a whole postseason, maybe, just maybe, the Heat can return to the NBA Finals for the first time since 2023.

title: Jack Bech, Hunter Nourzad, and Jacob Rodriguez are Week 11’s underrated AFC standouts
summary: Superstars may lead the discussion when it comes to success in the NFL, but more often than not, it’s the guys you barely know who will make the plays needed when they’re needed. Such players can be underrated for all kinds of reasons. Perhaps they’re playing in a smaller market, and the media isn’t appropriately […]
content: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images | Getty Images Superstars may lead the discussion when it comes to success in the NFL, but more often than not, it’s the guys you barely know who will make the plays needed when they’re needed. Such players can be underrated for all kinds of reasons. Perhaps they’re playing in a smaller market, and the media isn’t appropriately trumpeting their exploits. Maybe they’re hidden in a depth chart behind bigger names who may not be doing as much. Or, it’s always possible that a wayward coach hasn’t quite figured out that one guy needs elevation to bring better results to the team. Whatever the reason, we at SB Nation always like to bring the underrated names to you with the offseason Hidden Gems and in-season Secret Superstars series. You can also catch up on the AFC and NFC Secret Superstars for the 2026 season right here . Here are our AFC Secret Superstars for Week 11 of the 2026 regular season. And if you haven’t yet, download the new SB Nation app , so you can better read our stuff and join the conversation wherever you are! (All advanced metrics courtesy of Next Gen Stats , Pro Football Focus , Sports Info Solutions , and Sumer Sports unless otherwise indicated). Jack Bech, WR, Las Vegas Raiders Fernando Mendoza’s first road NFL start was no easier than his first home NFL start. After facing Mike Macdonald’s Seattle Seahawks’ defense in a 21-13 Week 10 loss, Mendoza and the Raiders had to travel to Denver to face Vance Joseph’s equally venomous Broncos defense last Sunday. And for the most part, the 2026 first overall pick acquitted himself well, completing 18 of 37 passes for 267 yards, three touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 88.5. All this without tight end Brock Bowers, the Raiders’ best target, who was out with ankle and quadriceps injuries. One reason it still worked without Bowers was the emergence of receiver Jack Bech, the 2025 second-round pick out of TCU, who put up career highs in targets (nine), catches (eight), and receiving yards (88) in a 38-24 loss that was closer than the final score suggests. The Raiders trailed by just seven until cornerback Ja’Quan McMillian’s 35-yard pick-six with 1:52 left What a snag by Ja'Quan McMillian 🔥 LVvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2niarbeNHE — NFL (@NFL) November 23, 2026 When Bech caught a seven-yard touchdown from Mendoza with 4:29 remaining, that put the score at 31-24 in Denver’s favor, but the Raiders had a shot to tie things up before the pick-six basically ended the game. Throughout this contest, Bech did a great job of replicating Bowers’ effectiveness in certain concepts — posts and over routes, safety-beaters up the seam, and the occasional two-man route in right spaces. The 6’2”. 215-pound Bech basically proved that when the plays call for that bigger contested catch receiver, and the team’s best bigger contested catch receiver is not on the field, he can pick up the slack. It’s something that Bech’s coaches and teammates have never doubted, and have been waiting for. The @Raiders had a chance against the @Broncos without Brock Bowers in part because Jack Bech acted as Bowers' stunt double. pic.twitter.com/LBbSeWCkH2 — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) November 23, 2026 “He’s always been gritty, always been a great teammate,” Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said of Bech postgame. “Then you get opportunities against a really good defense, and he made plays. So I’m happy for him. I’m not surprised. He makes those plays in practice, and with Brock out, he gets opportunities to go produce.” “Jack is a great guy,” Mendoza concluded. “He’s one of my best friends on the team. I have a lot of great friends on the team, and he’s someone who is notorious for staying after practice, catching extra balls. He’s been a fantastic player and teammate as well, so when he gets the attention, he rises to the occasion. Sometimes as a receiver it’s tough because they cover you, or the coverage they play doesn’t allow your route to be open. “So whenever that happens, he still has a great smile, and attitude, and a will to win.” Maybe with Bech and Bowers on the field together, there can be more smiles in a passing game that seems to be catching a bit of fire. Hunter Nourzad, OG, Kansas City Chiefs Atter years of waiting on an explosive offense, and winning Super Bowls with spit and baling wire on that side of the ball, the Kansas City Chiefs are quite relieved to have an offense that is an absolute wagon once again. Sunday’s 34-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals put Kansas City at 8-2 on the season (just behind the aforementioned Broncos in the AFC West), and it was Patrick Mahomes’ second game in a row with at least 300 passing yards and at least three touchdowns — something he hasn’t done since Weeks 10-11 of the 2022 season. One thing the Chiefs would need to overcome in this game was the loss of right guard Trey Smith to the concussion he suffered in Week 10’s 35-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons. A rough blow to the offensive line, but as it turned out, Andy Reid and offensive line coach Andy Heck had the right man as Next Man Up — 2024 fifth-round pick Hunter Nourzad out of Penn State. Against the Cardinals, Nourzad allowed one quarterback hit and no other pressures on 47 pass-blocking reps, and he was an absolute killer in the run game, with several force-multiplier blocks both at the first and second levels, and at both right guard (67 total snaps) and center (five total snaps). All this, by the way, without running back Kenneth Walker III, who was out with a groin injury. Recent Secret Superstar Emmett Johnson was the man once again, with 105 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries. . @Chiefs RG Trey Smith was out with a concussion, so KC asked Hunter Nourzad to deliver a similar level of violence. Nourzad had no problem delivering. pic.twitter.com/UemvDwTHRO — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) November 23, 2026 “I thought Hunter went out there and did a heck of a job,” offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy said on Monday . “He’s been working his tail off since he got here… Was it perfect? No. Did he have his fair share of mistakes? Yes… We still have got a lot of things that we have to clean up. I thought the communication was good up front, and the guys played well together.” Obviously, the hope is that Smith is back for the Chiefs’ pivotal Thanksgiving Day tilt against the Buffalo Bills, but if not, Nourzad appears to have this thing in the bag. And if Smith is ready to go, Nourzad’s performance gives the team flexibility it didn’t have before. Jacob Rodriguez, LB, Miami Dolphins Here’s a sentence that’s going to sound nuts to a lot of people: You might want to keep an eye on the Miami Dolphins’ rookie class on defense. Yes, the 2026 Dolphins are 1-9 on the season following Sunday’s 26-9 loss to the Buffalo Bills, and yes, they allowed 405 total net yards in that game, but hey — you need baby steps when your team is involved in 2026’s most obvious “clear the decks” restructuring . First-year head coach Jeff Hafley has proven that he knows how to match scheme and personnel defensively, and in conjunction with first-year general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan, these rebuilding ‘Fins are seeing the rewards from a great draft class sooner than they may have imagined. Between cornerback Chris Johnson, safety Michael Taaffe, and linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, the Dolphins’ rookies already have seven interceptions on the season, which is more than 11 teams have, regardless of draft class. Of those players, it’s Rodriguez who may be the most important. The Dolphins stole him with the 43rd overall pick in the second round out of Texas Tech — and I say “stole” because I got to watch tape with Rodriguez before the draft, and he broke it all down like a sure first-rounder . This season, Rodriguez has a sack, four pressures, 32 solo tackles, 38 stops, four tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. In coverage, he’s allowed 35 catches on 39 targets for 327 yards, two touchdowns, two interceptions (including one against the Bills), and an opponent passer rating of 97.3. The two touchdowns he allowed both came in Week 5 against the Cincinnati Bengals, and who hasn’t given up at least two touchdowns to Joe Burrow and his gang these days? Most importantly for the team is how Rodriguez is able to read and react to everything he sees. It jumped out with his college tape, and it’s been the same in the NFL. Over and over, Rodriguez was able to create stops against Buffalo’s explosive offense because he knew what was going on, and what his role was in it. Go ahead and tell me that Jacob Rodriguez is a five-year NFL veteran. I'd be inclined to believe you. pic.twitter.com/DSWHCdJPn7 — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) November 23, 2026 “I mean, to us it feels normal,” Rodriguez said on Nov. 18, when asked about this young defense coming into shape. “We didn’t know any other way. You know what I mean? We didn’t see it any other way. This is just what was asked of us, and what we’re trying to do the best in our jobs to do. I think that’s where we took it — we have a job to do, and we’re going to try to do our best to do the job as well as we can.” So, yeah… this isn’t a one-year thing, but again, this young defense is one to watch. Right now, and well into the future.

title: NFL survivor picks, strategy: Week 12 safe, value, and trap options
summary: Happy Thanksgiving! Even if you don’t celebrate the holiday, you know that it means a Thursday tripleheader of NFL action. The NFL has added a Black Friday game in recent years and now we also get a Wednesday game because the NFL clearly needs more revenue. Last week was a relatively quiet one, with few […]
content: (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Happy Thanksgiving! Even if you don’t celebrate the holiday, you know that it means a Thursday tripleheader of NFL action. The NFL has added a Black Friday game in recent years and now we also get a Wednesday game because the NFL clearly needs more revenue. Last week was a relatively quiet one, with few competitive matchups and the best game of the week, Vikings vs. 49ers in Mexico City, ending up a lopsided Niners win. The hope is this week brings something a little better, and the matchups on tap suggest it should. The week opens on Wednesday with two 6-4 squads as the Rams host the Packers. Thanksgiving brings us a huge NFC matchup between the Bears and Lions and a huge AFC matchup between the Chiefs and Bills. Black Friday features Broncos-Steelers with AFC seeding implications. Sunday brings Seahawks-49ers, and we close things out with the NFC South on Monday featuring Panthers vs. Buccaneers in Tampa. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and comments Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . I’m back with my Week 12 Survivor picks on Wednesday ahead of Packers-Rams. Survivor involves picking one team each week to win. If they win you advance, if they lose you’re out in most cases. I’m in one pool with four entries, but it’s also a double-elimination pool. I’m down to one entry that has one strike against it, but I’m hanging around for now. Below I’ve got a look at the safest choices, best value picks, and then trap picks. I’ll post my own picks at the end. I’ll update on Sunday once I lock in my three picks for the weekend. I’ve included odds for the favorite in each game, courtesy of FanDuel . Safest picks Jaguars (-14.5) over Titans Bengals (-9.5) over Saints The Jaguars are the biggest favorite this week, and it’s not close. The Bengals are the second biggest favorites and with the Saints struggling, they should roll. Best value picks Cowboys (-8.5) over Eagles Jaguars (-14.5) over Titans Cowboys over Eagles is very much a trap game (see below), but at this stage of the season, there’s value in them if you wanna get a little nuts. The only game you might use them is Week 17 at home against the Giants, but that would be arguably a wilder pick given the Giants performances this season. Avoid this pick if you can, but there’s some value if you are in a pickle. The Jaguars offer some value late in the season, traveling to face a bad Colts team in Week 18, but that’s a long ways off. First, you might not even make it to Week 18. Second, who knows what the Jaguars will or won’t have to play for and if they’ll even be playing starters. If you have them available, now is the week. Trap pick Cowboys (-8.5) over Eagles While there is some value, this is a tricky one given the divisional nature, the Eagles coming off a spicy win over the Steelers, and it being Thanksgiving. And the Cowboys remain a questionable option most weeks. My picks this week I’m rolling with the Jaguars.

title: Aaron Rodgers is throwing an epic temper tantrum over Steelers QB switch
summary: In an absolutely stunning move that nobody possibly could have seen coming, Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers isn’t handling being benched well at all. Not only is Rodgers throwing a tantrum over the team’s move to start Mason Rudolph in an attempt to spark their offense, but he’s simply not showing up for work at all. […]
content: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images In an absolutely stunning move that nobody possibly could have seen coming, Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers isn’t handling being benched well at all. Not only is Rodgers throwing a tantrum over the team’s move to start Mason Rudolph in an attempt to spark their offense, but he’s simply not showing up for work at all. This comes from veteran Steelers reporter Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, who said drama between the team and Rodgers had been simmering “for a while,” and that Rodgers didn’t report to the facility on Wednesday after the team announced it would start Rudolph on Tuesday night . There is a very real chance we won’t see Rodgers play again this season, perhaps at all. It’s been a rough transition at quarterback over the years for the Steelers, who moved on from Big Ben and ended up with Big Baby. It has been Rodgers’ modus operandi to claim the notion that he creates drama is simply a figment of the media’s imagination — while simultaneously spending each offseason playing the “will he or won’t he retire” game on The Pat McAfee Show , and now refusing to be a part of the team when head coach Mike McCarthy is trying to throw anything against the wall to make it stick. With the possibility of the playoffs waning, the organization could either continue with the status quo, or attempt to do something , and Rodgers was an obvious reason this team has struggled offensively. A glance at his overall stats might trick you into thinking Rodgers has been good this season, throwing for over 2,200 yards, 16 touchdowns, and 6 interceptions — but in reality, he’s been atrocious. Rodgers has averaged 2.4 completed air yards per pass this season. Only 876 yards passing have come in the air this season for him. His passing success rate is an abysmal 39%. Rodgers also hovers around an 80 in passer index, where 100 is rated as average — meaning he’s lagging behind a replacement-level QB. All this while being unable to generate explosive plays through the air, requiring his receivers to do everything with YAC. This has all led to the Steelers having the 22nd-ranked scoring offense in the NFL, and 22nd in passing yards — despite having the 8th most attempts in the league. Rodgers is cooked, it’s that simple. We all know Mason Rudolph isn’t the answer, but kudos to the Steelers for choosing not to settle for mediocrity just to keep Rodgers happy. The way he’s literally taken his ball and gone home, rather than help prepare Rudolph, or simply be there as part of the team, shows the incredible difference in character between Rodgers and someone like Kirk Cousins who took his veteran benching with grace in Atlanta, and understood his role as a mentor with the Falcons, then again in Las Vegas. If this is the end of the road for Aaron Rodgers’ NFL career, it will be remembered in two chapters: One as a Hall of Fame quarterback with the Packers who was one of the most efficient passers of the modern era, then whatever the hell the last four years have been, tarnishing his legacy and establishing him as one of the most self-centered egotists in football.

title: Aaron Rodgers blasts Mike McCarthy in Pat McAfee interview, gets released by Steelers
summary: UPDATE: Following his appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show,” Aaron Rodgers has been released by the Pittsburgh Steelers. The football world woke up Wednesday morning to the news that the Pittsburgh Steelers were starting Mason Rudolph on Friday against the Denver Broncos, and that the franchise would make veteran Aaron Rodgers inactive for the Black […]
content: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images UPDATE: Following his appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show,” Aaron Rodgers has been released by the Pittsburgh Steelers. The football world woke up Wednesday morning to the news that the Pittsburgh Steelers were starting Mason Rudolph on Friday against the Denver Broncos, and that the franchise would make veteran Aaron Rodgers inactive for the Black Friday contest. Rodgers then took to the airwaves of his favorite sports show, “The Pat McAfee Show,” Wednesday afternoon to air his side of the story. And the results were stunning. At the outset, Rodgers stated that this has been “months of conversations leading up to the last couple of days.” According to Rodgers, head coach Mike McCarthy did not inform him that he was benched; instead, he learned it from tight end Pat Freiermuth during a phone call on Tuesday evening. “I didn’t hear from Mike, wrapping up our conversation that we had [Tuesday night] at about 6:15, 6:30,” added Rodgers. “Still haven’t heard from people there.” Rodgers also alleged that McCarthy slept through several meetings, was snoring during one meeting, and missed others. “Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down, and within ten minutes began snoring. Woke himself up, was rattling his papers, we all looked around, five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. Less than five minutes after that he walks out of the room like nothing happened,” said Rodgers. “Thursday he misses an offensive meeting. Friday, he doesn’t come to the first walkthrough, doesn’t come to the protection walkthrough on Thursday … we don’t have a team meeting on Saturday night in Philly.” Rodgers also alleged that there were some defensive guys that “didn’t like the way things were going,” and said the “nail in the coffin” came when McCarthy broke down the team at halftime in Philadelphia against the Eagles with a “one-two-three-Packers” chant. According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, that story is true, per his sources: I have confirmed the Mike McCarthy “1, 2, 3 PACKERS!” story is true, per multiple sources. https://t.co/YdWwTao4l8 — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 25, 2026 The quarterback then said the conversations with McCarthy wore on over months, and that Rodgers began the discussions with McCarthy first as a “concerned friend.” He also said that he felt the team needed to make a change in playcalling “for the betterment of the team.” “Everybody knows what’s going on,” continued Rodgers. “At some point, people are going to learn exactly what’s going on — and it’s crazy.” The quarterback added that “[a]t this point, I’m not going back to Pittsburgh. That ship has sailed.” He also brought up his feelings on the. COVID-19 pandemic and vaccine, again, and his frustrations with the “people who railed against me.” You can see the entire segment of Rodgers’ allegations here: Aaron Rodgers on the Pat McAfee show pic.twitter.com/ZdgCtHPmSq — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 25, 2026 One thing is for sure. This will not be the end of the story in Pittsburgh.

title: NWSL growth impossible to ignore after 14th season conclusion
summary: The 2026 NWSL season has officially concluded after the Kansas City Current took home the championship following a 2-1 win over the Washington Spirit. As the league begins its shortest offseason ever, the focus shifts to kicking off a 15th season. The league first began play in 2013, a year after Women’s Professional Soccer folded. […]
content: Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images | Getty Images The 2026 NWSL season has officially concluded after the Kansas City Current took home the championship following a 2-1 win over the Washington Spirit. As the league begins its shortest offseason ever, the focus shifts to kicking off a 15th season. The league first began play in 2013, a year after Women’s Professional Soccer folded. The NWSL started off as the third professional women’s soccer league to exist in the United States. After both of its predecessors failed due to high operating costs, the league implemented a strict salary cap of $200,000 per team. The league minimum salary was $6,000 a year, and no player was allowed to make more than $30,000. Salaries across the league were subsidized by the federation-allocated players mechanism, wherein those playing internationally for the US, Canada, or Mexico were paid by their national federations rather than their clubs. In 2027, NWSL teams will be bound by a base salary cap of at least $4.4 million, although it will vary from club to club based on expansion allocation money, the high impact player rule and revenue sharing. No player will be making less than $65,000—equivalent to around $45,000 in 2013—and the league has not had a maximum salary in place since the start of the 2024 season. Since the signing of a historic collective bargaining agreement (CBA) in August 2024, all players now get to enjoy unrestricted free agency, including those beginning their professional careers after college as the college draft was also abolished. Across its first 14 seasons, the NWSL has become an exponentially more viable and sustainable place for players to pursue careers as professional athletes. It has also become a friendlier place for players to pursue parenthood without risking their careers. Washington Spirit forward Ashley Hatch, who recently returned to play after giving birth to her son, Leo, in January of this year, emphasized: “I don’t think I would have been able to go through it if it wasn’t for the CBA. Knowing that I had massive job security, it was the main reason why I felt like I could do it.” The league has also grown leaps and bounds in terms of its audience and visibility. The inaugural NWSL season saw an average attendance of just over 4,000 spectators. Removing the outlier Portland Thorns, who averaged over 13,000 fans a match, the league’s average attendance was under 3,000. Moreover, only 4,200 fans were there to watch the league’s second-ever championship game. This weekend, the NWSL Championship was played in front of a sold out crowd for the third consecutive year. Average attendances across the season have not dipped below 10,000 since the 2023 season, and a record 2,643,616 fans watched their favorite clubs play live in 2026. Even the four years since the championship game was last played at Audi Field in Washington, D.C. have seen immense growth. NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman pointed out in her annual State of the League address ahead of the final game that total attendance has grown by 154 percent in those four years and that the salary cap has gone up by 236 percent. Berman also pointed to the monetary growth that the league has experienced, which is particularly important given that previous attempts at professional women’s soccer leagues in the U.S. failed due to financial instability. “Ironically, it was Michele Kang who bought the Washington Spirit [in 2022] for just $35 million,” she started. “At that time, many people were wondering how that investment could make any sense. This year, we sold team number 18 to Columbus for $205 million, a 486% increase in team value. “In 2022, we had zero stadiums purpose built for women, not just in the NWSL but in the world. And now we have CPKC Stadium… and they’re going to be expanding the capacity of that building to 18,000 because they have actually sold out each and every game.” Infrastructure has improved massively not just for fans but for the players themselves. When the league first kicked off, zero clubs had dedicated training facilities. Today, nearly three-quarters of the teams in the league train or will soon train at facilities purpose built for them. Despite these notable improvements, there is still plenty of room to grow as the NWSL enters year 15. The semifinals and final of the playoffs this year were marred by controversy surrounding scheduling, as clubs continued to be treated as second-class citizens in their home stadiums. Infrastructure and resources are far from standardized across the league; Washington Spirit defender Casey Krueger identified “across the board, making sure that every single team has the same level of support” as a priority for the league. Finally, in order to remain a top destination for top players around the world, the league needs to adjust salary mechanisms in order to match the wages offered by top clubs abroad.
